cross_worker_reconciliation.issue_1_slot_shape: RESOLVED — CONSISTENT. The canonical shape is top-level day[slot_id] keys (e.g. day.breakfast, day.morning_activity). Verified in three places: (1) schemas/v2/day.schema.json line 53-66 defines 'slots' as a nested object with the 6 named slots, BUT save.py _apply_select_mutation writes day.setdefault(slot_id, ...) at TOP LEVEL (not day.slots). (2) state.js _getSlotByKey reads day.slots[slotId] first (nested), then day[slotId] (top-level) as fallback — handles both shapes for hydration back-compat. (3) requestSelectMutation optimistically writes day[slotId] at top-level to match save.py post-save shape. The schema allows the nested 'slots' key for JSON Schema validation purposes, but the runtime path (save.py + state.js) uses top-level. No fix required; M4b's dual-shape reader already handles this. QA note: when testing hydration, days may arrive in either shape depending on whether they were written by save.py (top-level) or by the fixture builder (may use nested). state.js handles both.
cross_worker_reconciliation.issue_2_export_gating: CONFIRMED PRESENT. renderExportButtons() in web/js/state.js (lines 457-467) gates export on three conditions: (1) !_anyValidationError() — _anyValidationError() calls _allRequiredSlotsFilled(day) for every day, which checks all required slots have selected_option_id; (2) state.days.every(d => ['user-selected','timeline','transportation','finalized'].includes(d.stage)) — all days must be at or past user-selected stage; (3) !state.ui.offline. Both export buttons (PDF + iCal) are disabled when any condition fails. This implements the Approve-gate check. Hard validation errors (unfilled required slots) disable Export before POST /api/export/* is called. No fix required.
